endpoint: Change in quantitative CT fibrosis extent (data-driven texture or e-Lung style automated scores)
why_needed: No endpoint in the record measures whether fibrosis regresses. FVC can rise for reasons unrelated to fibrosis (effort, weight, comorbid resolution) and cannot distinguish arrest from reversal.
approach: Paired quantitative CT at baseline and 12 months with a prespecified regression threshold defined as a decrease in fibrosis extent exceeding measurement error, established from same-day repeat scans.
existing_validation: Quantitative CT scores are associated with outcomes in fibrotic ILD cohorts (for example the e-Lung biomarker literature), but no published threshold for regression exists and no trial has used regression as an endpoint.
feasibility: High: uses scans already acquired in most trials and registries.
smallest_validation_step: Retrospective application to an existing trial or registry image set with same-day repeat scans, to estimate measurement error and the proportion of patients showing change beyond it. No new patient contact required.

endpoint: Sustained FVC improvement of at least 5% predicted maintained for at least 6 months
why_needed: Trials report mean change and categorical decline thresholds; a durable improvement category is almost never prespecified, so the record cannot say how often improvement occurs or whether any treatment increases it.
approach: Prespecified responder analysis requiring two consecutive measurements at least 6 months apart both above the baseline threshold, with sensitivity analysis for measurement variability.
existing_validation: Categorical decline thresholds are validated prognostically (PMID 40020995); the mirror-image improvement category has no comparable validation.
feasibility: High: computable from existing trial datasets without new measurement.
smallest_validation_step: Re-analysis of completed placebo-controlled trial datasets to estimate the background rate of sustained improvement under placebo and under active treatment. This is a data-request and re-analysis step, not a new trial.

endpoint: Time to sustained improvement in gas transfer (DLco) beyond measurement error
why_needed: DLco is usually a secondary endpoint reported as mean change; the record contains no intervention with evidence of DLco recovery, and it is unknown whether the absence reflects biology or measurement practice.
approach: Repeat-measurement error model from within-subject same-visit duplicates, then a time-to-event analysis of first sustained improvement above that error.
existing_validation: DLco decline thresholds are prognostically validated in registry data (PMID 40020995).
feasibility: Moderate: requires duplicate-measurement data, which few datasets retain.
smallest_validation_step: Estimate within-visit DLco reproducibility in one existing cohort with duplicate measurements before proposing the endpoint for any trial.

endpoint: Six-month survival free of acute exacerbation after a first exacerbation
dimension: durable benefit after an acute event
why_needed: The only positive randomised survival signal in the record (STRIVE-IPF) uses six-month survival after an exacerbation, and no comparable endpoint is standardised, so the signal cannot be compared with anything.
approach: Composite of survival and freedom from a further adjudicated exacerbation, with blinded adjudication against consensus exacerbation criteria.
existing_validation: Exacerbation criteria are consensus-defined but adjudication practice varies between trials; the composite itself is unvalidated.
feasibility: Moderate: needs adjudication infrastructure but no new measurement technology.
smallest_validation_step: Apply the composite retrospectively to the two registered exacerbation trials and to STRIVE-IPF's own data once the analysis is released (action A10), to establish event rates and adjudication agreement.

endpoint: Patient-reported functional recovery anchored to a measured activity threshold
dimension: symptoms and function, anchored rather than self-referential
why_needed: Symptom instruments in the record (SGRQ-I, K-BILD, cough scores) measure change in reported state but are not anchored to any measured capacity, so symptom improvement cannot be separated from expectation effects in unblinded studies, which is precisely the weakness of the record's open-label positive signals.
approach: Pair an instrument change with a concurrently measured objective anchor (actigraphy step count or a standardised walk test) and define recovery as improvement in both.
existing_validation: Both components are individually used in IPF trials; the paired definition is not validated.
feasibility: High: actigraphy and walk tests are already collected in many trials.
smallest_validation_step: Correlate existing paired instrument and actigraphy data in a completed trial or registry to determine whether an anchored definition is achievable at all.
